title: Synthesis of Near-Infrared Emitting Gold Nanoclusters for Biological Applications
protocol: Add 7.8 mg thioctic acid and 60 μL of 2 M NaOH to 23.4 mL ultrapure water.
Stir the mixture until thioctic acid dissolves completely (~15-20 min).
Sonicate the mixture for faster dissolution if needed.
Add 10.2 μL of HAuCl4·3H2O aqueous solution to the dissolved thioctic acid mixture.
After 15 minutes, add 480 μL of NaBH4 (1.9 mg/mL) under vigorous stirring.
Stir the reaction mixture overnight under vigorous stirring conditions.
Purify the solution by applying three cycles of centrifugation/filtration using a membrane filtration device with a molecular weight cut-off of 3 kDa.
Add thiol-terminated polyethylene glycol (MW 2,000; 15.6 mg) to the purified AuNCs solution.
Adjust the pH to 7-7.5 and stir the mixture overnight.
Purify the dispersion by applying three cycles of centrifugation/filtration using a membrane filtration device with a molecular weight cut-off of 3 kDa.
Adjust the pH to 4.5 with 1 M HCl.
Add 3-(aminopropyl)triphenylphosphonium bromide (TPP) to the mixture.
Start the reaction by adding N-(3-dimethyl-aminopropyl)-N′-ethylcarbodiimide hydrochloride (EDC·HCl).
Monitor and adjust pH as necessary to maintain between 4.5–6 using 1 M HCl.
Stir the reaction mixture overnight at room temperature.
Purify the dispersion by applying three cycles of centrifugation/filtration using a membrane filtration device with a molecular weight cut-off of 3 kDa.
Dilute the purified solution with ultrapure water to the initial volume of 24 mL.
Culture HeLa cells in Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s Medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum in 5% CO2 at 37 °C.
Split and passage the cells when they reach ~80% confluence.
Seed HeLa cells in a 12-well plate at a density of 20,000 cells/mL (1 mL/well).
Incubate the seeded cells for 48 hours to achieve approximately 50% confluence.
Aspirate the culture medium after 48 hours post-seeding.
Add 400 μL of complete culture medium to untreated control wells.
Mix 500 μg of nanoparticles with 400 μL of complete culture medium for treated samples.
Return cultures to a 37 °C incubator after adding the solutions.
Concentrate AuNC solution obtained in step 2.4 by 100 times, resulting in 40 mL concentrated to 400 μL.
Add 25 μL of this concentrated solution to 400 μL cell culture media for treated samples.
Incubate the cells with the solutions for 2 hours.
Detach the cells using standard trypsinization according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Collect detached cells in polypropylene microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge collected samples at 350 x g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Prepare FCM buffer by supplementing pre-chilled PBS with 2% bovine serum albumin at 4 °C.
Wash the cell pellets with 1 mL of FCM buffer.
Centrifuge washed cells at 350 x g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL of FCM buffer.
Store resuspended samples at 4 °C prior to analysis.
Filter all samples using a 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tube with a cell-strainer cap.
Specify the cytometer configuration before acquiring data using the instrument software.
Format all dot-plots and histograms for ‘Acquisitions’.
Plot a two-parameter dot plot of forward scatter area (FSC-A) vs. side scatter area (SSC-A) to show distribution of cells.
Create a two-parameter dot plot of FSC height (FSC-H) vs. FSC-A to exclude doublets.
Plot a single-parameter histogram for the fluorescent channel area (FL-A) to monitor relative fluorescence intensity in the sample.
Use a linear scale to depict FSC and SSC data.
Use a logarithmic scale for all fluorescent parameters.
Acquire untreated sample at a low flow rate to minimize coincident events.
Adjust photomultiplier tube (PMT) voltages during acquisition to get the untreated population on scale on the FSC vs SSC plot.
Adjust PMT voltages for the FL channel if necessary to place the unstained population on the left corner of the histogram.
Select the specific ‘gate tab’ in the software and draw an appropriate gate around the desired population.
Record 10,000 events per sample.
Record all samples under the same instrument settings.
Use an appropriate program to analyze the flow cytometry data.
Seed HeLa cells onto a 4-chamber glass bottom 35 mm dish at a density of 250,000 cells/mL (0.5 mL/chamber).
Incubate the seeded cells in a 37 °C incubator with 5% CO2 atmosphere to achieve ~50% confluence after 24 h.
Add 100 µg of AuNCs or 10 µL from the stock solution of 10 mg/mL to each dish chamber containing 0.5 mL of medium with cells (for treated samples).
Incubate the dish in a 37 °C incubator for 24 h.
Discard the medium and wash the cells with pre-warmed fresh medium for 5 min.
Repeat the washing step once more.
Fill each chamber with 800 µL of fresh medium prior to CLSM imaging.
Mount the dish on the microscope inverted stage with the chamber warmed to 37 °C and supplied with humidified 5% CO2 atmosphere.
Use a 405 nm laser set at 2% power with an appropriate beam splitter.
Set the range of detection wavelengths between 650 and 760 nm.
Set the resolution of the image to 2048 x 2048 pixels.
Aim for a pixel dwell time around 4 µs in the acquisition speed setting.
Acquire the image with 2x averaging (line mode, averaging method mean).
Set the pinhole to 1 Airy unit (for 405 nm light).
Use photon-counting mode for higher sensitivity.
Use Köhler’s setting of the condenser and the field stop for correct illumination in transmitted light with differential interference contrast (DIC).
Use a 488 nm laser at 0.7% power without any fluorescence detector assigned for acquisition of transmitted light.
Set an appropriate beam splitter for the laser wavelength.
Acquire two images for each track (red fluorescence and DIC).
